historical_record.description: The Noe Valley Branch Library was built, the third of San Francisco's seven Carnegie-funded branch libraries: brick in a tapestry bond with polychrome glazed terra cotta, one storey over a raised basement, a stair rising from a small vestibule into the main reading room.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 259, Carnegie Noe Valley/Sally Brunn Branch Library.
A community deck designed by architect Al Lanier was built with help from Friends of Noe Valley behind the library's children's room and christened on July 4, 1980.
A mural painted by an artist and neighborhood children on the east fence of the Noe Valley Library was dedicated on November 10, 1990.
The branch library, newly renamed for Sally Brunn, held a dedication ceremony and nameplate installation.
The terraced community garden behind the Noe Valley Library was built in 1976 by Friends of Noe Valley.
The library's community garden reopened after being closed for two years, largely because of the drought.
The Noe Valley branch library closed on Feb. 11, 2006 for a seismic renovation, with a farewell party.
The Noe Valley branch library reopened with a dedication ceremony after a two-year, $5.7 million seismic and other renovation.
The preservation architects Carey & Co. presented their design for the branch's renovation to the Library Commission's peer review panel.
